title: Natural direct-image identification of tensor-sections sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:X.Opens\to X.Etale$ a continuous functor whose composite with the forgetful functor equals $X.restrictFunctor$. Put $T=i_*$, the sectionwise continuous direct image [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For quasi-coherent modules $F,G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], let $m(F,G,\varphi):F_{et}\to G_{et}$ have components $\Gamma(U,u^*\varphi)$ for the tensor-sections sheaves [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. Then there are simultaneously sheaf isomorphisms $a_F:F_{ab}\cong T(F_{et})$ with $\varphi_{ab};a_G=a_F;T(m(F,G,\varphi))$. This is an underived sheaf identification and makes no cohomological assertion.

proof.text: Use the explicitly constructed unit-normalized tensor-to-restriction open-section isomorphisms. Naturality in the coefficient module follows by applying the natural transformation leftAdjointUniq to the module map, evaluating on the top open, and commuting the final image-top transport with the underlying additive presheaf map. Equality transports between over-scheme objects commute with tensor-pullback maps by equality elimination.

Restriction compatibility assembles those component isomorphisms into a natural isomorphism of presheaves. Lift its inverse to a sheaf isomorphism using full faithfulness of sheafToPresheaf. Apply the prescribed component formula for m and the coefficient naturality square; cancel the invertible open-section comparison to prove the asserted sheaf naturality.
